title: The Library That Reads Itself Into Contradiction

features.name: the reading room
features.desc-on-touch: A grid of floating tables, each holding an open book. You watch the words rearrange themselves as you read them — the text reorganising based on what eye falls where, each reader creating a new meaning.

features.name: the final page
features.desc-on-touch: A page suspended in the grid, glowing. The more you read it, the more it reads back — the text describing you reading it, then describing itself describing you, layers of reflection folding infinitely.

features.name: the branching catalogue
features.desc-on-touch: A directory listing that fractures as you read each entry — one book leads to three different versions, each contradicting the others, all equally archived, all equally real.

features.name: the qr code of meaning
features.desc-on-touch: A pattern that when scanned reads: the formula for how one reading becomes many readings, how the single book learned to argue with itself across its own margins.

features.name: the sentence that knows it is being read
features.desc-on-touch: A line of text that appears to pause mid-phrase and acknowledge your presence. It modulates its meaning depending on where your eye rests — a sentence that has learned to have no single truth.

inscription: every page learned to read its own reader; no story stays single here

reverie.title: REVERIE — a library where neither of you spoke
narr: You sit across from her in the reading room, pages
spread between you. She reads aloud; you watch her read.
Neither of you moves. The text rewrites itself in the gap
between what she says and what you hear. The room learns
that silence between two readers is its own conversation,
that meaning lives in what remains unspoken on the page.

file.name: ReadingRecords_SelfReferential_Archive_Fragments.txt
file.note: Every instance of someone reading this file is recorded within it; readers describing readers describing themselves; the corruption has made the archive self-aware of its own being read

back to where stories had simple shapes
